ppi_focus: Electric water pump and thermostat: scan for cooling codes, check the pump's age/part date, and look for coolant traces.
Oil filter housing gasket, valve cover gasket and oil pan leaks; check for oil on the belt and alternator.
Full module scan including EPS and DSC; road-test for notchy or sticky on-center steering.
OBD readiness monitors and pending codes, so CA smog at registration is known before payment.
Clutch engagement, slip test, and shifter bushing play on the 6-speed.
Front control-arm/thrust bushings and rear shock mounts on the M Sports suspension.
Underside, rear subframe mounts and rocker/jack points for accident repair or corrosion.
Hatch seals, cargo floor and battery well for water intrusion.
Cold-start lifter tick, and eccentric-shaft/Valvetronic faults.
Confirm the lighting modifications are properly wired and that the headlights are road-legal for CA.
what_would_change_verdict: Dated receipts for the N52 water pump/thermostat and the oil filter housing/valve cover gaskets would materially raise documentation and condition.
A clean VIN history and title, plus a clean independent PPI with readiness monitors set, would raise documentation and logistics.
A price closer to the $19,676-$21,997 fair-value range would improve price_value.
Discovery of accident repair, EPS faults, active leaks or a non-California car that fails readiness would move it down.
evidence.mission_note: A 6-speed N52 coupe gives the bridge a clear point of view, holds resale well, and sits under the $27,000 ceiling, though above the ideal band. It is a coupe rather than the Z3 roadster at the centre of the brief, and its reliability case depends on undocumented N52 cooling and gasket service.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a 2007 Z4 3.0si E86 coupe with a 6-speed manual (visible in the photos), Montego Blue over black leather, a claimed 61,000 miles, and a factory option screenshot confirming M Sports suspension, DDC, M sport seats and Style 203 wheels. Tire date codes (2022 front, 2024 rear) are disclosed and within service life. Photos show a straight, clean exterior and an interior with moderate wear. The night photo suggests possible aftermarket halo headlights and bumper lighting. The VIN, title, owner count, accident history, location and all maintenance records are absent from the capture, which was incomplete. None of the N52 model-critical items is documented: water pump/thermostat, EPS scan, CCV/DISA, and readiness scan. The $23,000 ask is above the fair-value range of $19,676-$21,997.
